newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's Idemitsu finds new oil reserves off Norway.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Idemitsu finds new oil reserves off Norway.

text.p: Japanese refiner Idemitsu Kosan Co Ltd said on Tuesday it had confirmed oil reserves after test drilling in the North Sea off Norway.
Two promising formations were discovered in block 34/7, to which Idemitsu has concession rights of 9.6 percent.

One of the formations, located northeast of the Statfjord Nord field, will have an estimated output of 23,000 barrels per day (bpd), and output from the other, called the Southern Triangle Upper Jura and located southeast of the Tordis oil field, is estimated at 6,600 to 11,000 bpd, Idemitsu said.
The Southern Triangle Upper Jura formation is also expected to produce about 160,000 cubic metres of natural gas per day.
Recoverable reserves are estimated at about 40 million barrels for both formations, and commercial production is expected to begin within two to three years, Idemitsu said.

The discoveries are small in scale compared with other oil fields in the North Sea off Norway, but the economics of the project are very good because facilities from nearby oil fields currently in operation can be used, it said.
Main operators in the block are Norway's Den Norske Stats Oljeselskap A/S (Statoil), which has a 55.4 percent interest, and Saga Petroleum A/S, which has a 7.7 percent interest.
